crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Retrieval-Grounded Legal Research
children.blurb: Retrieval-grounded legal research is the practice of using AI systems that answer legal questions by first fetching relevant primary and secondary sources, then generating a response tied to those sources.

children.name: Adversarial Statutory Interpretation
children.blurb: Adversarial statutory interpretation is the practice of researching and arguing competing readings of a statute when parties have adverse legal interests.

children.name: Brief Drafting with Machine Assistance
children.blurb: Brief drafting with machine assistance covers the use of software to help produce legal briefs, motions, and memoranda for courts and clients.

children.name: Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking
children.blurb: Citation auditing and good law checking cover the verification of every authority cited in a brief, memo, opinion, or client advice, from case citations and pin cites to statutes, regulations, and secondary sources.

children.name: Jurisdictional Anomalies and Local Codes
children.blurb: Jurisdictional anomalies and local codes covers the places where AI rules do not line up: a state statute that conflicts with a city ordinance, a county procurement rule that reaches further than federal guidance, or a court rule that assumes a technology the local code never defines.

sections.body: Legal research and case strategy is the work of finding authority, reading statutes and rules closely, drafting arguments, and checking that every citation remains good law. AI systems now retrieve passages from case law, statutes, regulations, and secondary sources, then summarize or rank them for a human researcher. They can compare competing statutory readings, flag ambiguous language, and suggest counterarguments. They can draft sections of briefs, generate citation lists, and check whether a cited case has been overruled or questioned. The site tracks 148 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, which shows how quickly courts are generating new material for this kind of research. The output is still a draft or a lead, not a final legal conclusion.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Retrieval has improved because models can be grounded in a closed set of documents, so answers can point to sources instead of relying on memory. Citation auditing is partly solved for simple checks, such as whether a case exists and whether later cases cite it negatively, but it is not solved for subtle doctrinal shifts or unpublished dispositions. Adversarial statutory reading remains hard because a model can produce a plausible reading without understanding legislative history, agency practice, or local custom. Brief drafting is useful for structure, routine paragraphs, and alternative formulations, yet it still needs a lawyer to verify facts, tone, and strategy. The site tracks 29 AI case law precedents, a small but growing set that shows how courts are treating AI related questions. The honest limit is that no system can guarantee that a citation is good law in every jurisdiction or that a statutory argument will persuade a particular judge.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages move from finding authority to testing arguments to producing and checking work. Retrieval-Grounded Legal Research is the entry point for source based search and for understanding how grounding changes reliability. Adversarial Statutory Interpretation takes the next step, asking how a model can stress test a reading against text, structure, and purpose. Brief Drafting with Machine Assistance shows where generated prose fits into a larger argument and where human revision is still required. Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking covers the verification layer, including the risk of fabricated or outdated authority. Jurisdictional Anomalies and Local Codes addresses the fact that 6978 state AI bills and many local rules create a patchwork that no single model can master at once, so a reader would go to each page for a different part of the same workflow.
